overview.text: In a two-dimensional Cartesian (rectangular) coordinate plane, the origin is the point where the horizontal x-axis and vertical y-axis meet; its coordinates are written (0,0). Each zero means there is no displacement from the origin along that axis. The origin is the common reference point for locating others: an ordered pair (x,y) gives the horizontal displacement first and the vertical displacement second, with signs indicating direction. Because it lies on both axes, the origin is not in any of the four quadrants. It serves as the starting point for plotting locations and describing graphs in the plane.

key_facts.text: The origin is the intersection of the x- and y-axes, and its ordered pair is (0,0).
In an ordered pair (x,y), x comes first and represents horizontal displacement; y comes second and represents vertical displacement.
A point with x-coordinate 0 lies on the y-axis; a point with y-coordinate 0 lies on the x-axis. The origin lies on both.
The two axes divide the plane into four quadrants, so the origin, which lies on the axes, is not inside a quadrant.
The origin is a reference point: other points are located by their horizontal and vertical displacements from it.
